variables.name: TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS

readers.program: rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host and the tests that link the full or fake scheduler (model code in h/tron/models, compiled into the model objects of that scheduler)
readers.mechanism: getenv, then atol, in init_max_main_helpers(). The constructor of model::state calls it (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1615). Each full_scheduler owns one state (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1821 and :1830). get_scheduler builds the schedulers (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:64 and :80).

variables.values: Integer text parsed with atol. The result is stored as size_t (an unsigned type). The unit is worker threads of the shared app thread pool. atol accepts leading spaces and ignores text after the digits.
variables.default: Unset: half of the app pool workers, by integer division (h/tron/models/model.hpp:82). The app pool has the number of app CPUs minus 1 workers (h/tron/threading.hpp:754-755).
variables.empty_value: Parses as 0. The rule for 0 then applies: main helpers are off, and the process aborts if the minimum is above 0.
variables.invalid_value: Non-numeric text parses as 0. A negative number wraps to a very large unsigned value, so the variable then sets no upper limit. If the result is below the minimum (TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS or its default), TRON_ASSERT_LE at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1616 aborts the process when the scheduler is built, which is at model load. TRON_ASSERT is active in every build type (h/common/assert.hpp:3-5 and :69-75). It logs the message, logs 'Aborting.' and calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:57-63).
variables.effect: Sets the upper limit of main helpers in each forward pass. Main helpers are app pool workers that help the main thread with the non-attention work. The other pool workers run attention. The value 0 turns main helpers off (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2375-2376).
variables.interactions: TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS must not be above this value. On a pool of 16 or more workers the default minimum is 1 (h/tron/models/model.hpp:75-76), so TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS=0 alone aborts there. Set TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS=0 as well. The count of one pass is min(parallelism the model plugin reports, min(max, max(min, n))) (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2413-2415). With pay_for_determinism the fixed split (pool workers times 2, divided by 7) is still limited by this value (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2377-2382 and :2414). The comment at h/tron/models/model.hpp:2360-2365 says a change of the split changes the attention plan and the exact logits. The code does not limit the value to the pool size. The value is read again for each scheduler that is built. No command-line flag sets it. rinzler_proxy and rinzler_mock do not run this read: they have their own get_scheduler (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:87, src/tron/scheduler/mock.cpp:67).
variables.how_to_check: No log line or stat prints the value. If min is above max the abort message is 'TRON_ASSERT((min_main_helpers) <= (max_main_helpers)): Expected min_main_helpers <= max_main_helpers, but got <min> > <max>.' (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1616, h/common/assert.hpp:82-83). Indirect check: with TRON_ATTN_STATS on, the attention report holds n_attn_workers_min and n_attn_workers_max (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:768). The helpers of a pass are the pool workers minus the attention workers (h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:657).
variables.audience_reason: Performance tuning of rinzler and runtron: it limits how the worker threads are split between main work and attention.

variables.name: TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE

readers.program: t_prequant_cache only (a test). The function is defined in a product header, but no file under h/ or src/ includes that header or calls the function.

variables.values: Any non-empty text other than exactly 0 makes the function return true (cache disabled). The text is not parsed further (h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp:138).
variables.default: Unset: the function returns false (cache enabled).
variables.empty_value: Returns false (cache enabled), same as unset.
variables.invalid_value: There is no invalid value. Every non-empty text other than 0 counts as disabled, for example no or false (t/t_prequant_cache.cpp:542-545).
variables.effect: At this commit: no effect on rinzler, runtron or any other product program. Only the return value of prequant_cache_disabled() changes, and only the test t/t_prequant_cache.cpp calls it (lines 531-545). The prequant cache stores quantized model weights on disk so that a later load can read them back (h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp:3-9).
variables.interactions: h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp is included only by t/t_prequant_cache.cpp:44. The comment at h/tron/models/registry.hpp:47 says the prequant cache is to be enabled for model loads later. The cache root comes from POS_PREQUANT_CACHE, then POS_WEIGHTS_CACHE (h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp:141-151); those reads are also reached only from the test at this commit.
variables.how_to_check: none found. No product code reads the variable, so no log line or stat can show it.
variables.audience_reason: Neither operator nor developer-debug fits at this commit: only a test calls the reader. It becomes an operator switch when model loading calls prequant_cache_disabled().

variables.name: TRON_NO_RTM

readers.program: every program whose final link holds src/system/mwaitx.cpp (all that link the system library: rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, list_devices, tests; src/system/CMakeLists.txt:36-55)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then strcmp with 1, in rtm_disabled_by_env(). The only caller is the initializer of the namespace-scope constant is_rtm_supported (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:57-59). The type lazy<bool> runs its initializer in its constructor (h/common/util.hpp:200-205). The call is skipped when the CPU is not Intel or CPUID does not report RTM (short-circuit at :58).

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 turns RTM off. Every other text leaves RTM on (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:42).
variables.default: Unset: waits use Intel RTM (TSX, transactional memory instructions) when the CPU is Intel and CPUID reports RTM (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:47-59).
variables.empty_value: Same as unset: RTM stays on.
variables.invalid_value: Any text other than exactly 1 is ignored, for example true, yes, 01, or 1 followed by a space. RTM stays on. No message is printed.
variables.effect: On an Intel CPU with RTM, the wait code stops using RTM transactions. Each wait step is then a plain pause instruction (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:156-194). delay_ns then uses its time-stamp-counter spin loop for the last part of a delay (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:286-299). The startup banner says decode is 13 to 30 percent slower.
variables.interactions: No effect on AMD CPUs: the variable is not read there, and the AMD mwaitx path is used (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:133). No effect on an Intel CPU without RTM. The value is read before main starts, so it must be in the environment when the process starts. No command-line flag sets it. A test reads the same name with its own getenv (t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:239).
variables.how_to_check: system_init logs one of three texts, once (src/system/system.cpp:168). RTM in use: info line 'INIT: Intel RTM (TSX) supported' (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:68). Turned off by the variable: five error lines, with 'INIT: *** Intel RTM (TSX) DISABLED by TRON_NO_RTM=1   ***' (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:70-74). Intel CPU without RTM: warning 'INIT: Intel CPU without RTM (TSX): spin+pause fallback costs 13-30% decode; enable TSX ...' (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:76-77).
variables.audience_reason: The banner in the code says: benchmarking only, never production (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:73).

variables.name: TRON_PERF_INTERVAL_SEC

readers.program: rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host and the tests that link the full or fake scheduler (full scheduler code in h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then std::stof, in the initializer of a function-local static in scheduler_metrics_t::report_performance(). full_scheduler::forward() calls it after each forward pass that had token jobs (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2040; the early return at :2021-2027 skips it).

variables.values: Floating-point text parsed with std::stof. The unit is seconds. 0 means off. A positive value is the shortest time between two log lines. A negative value is not off: the log line is then written after every forward pass that did work (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:232).
variables.default: Unset: 0.0, so no log line is written (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:230 and :232).
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. std::stof throws std::invalid_argument on empty text, and the process ends (see invalid_value).
variables.invalid_value: Text that does not start with a number makes std::stof throw. report_performance() and forward() are declared noexcept (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:223 and :2012), so the exception ends the process. This happens at the end of the first forward pass that did work, so at the first request and not at startup.
variables.effect: When not 0, the scheduler writes one info log line after a forward pass when at least that many seconds have passed since the last line. The line gives the passes, tokens, logits, elapsed seconds and tokens per second of that interval. Each scheduler keeps its own counters (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:223-246).
variables.interactions: The value is read once per process and then kept. The line is written only when a forward pass ends, so an idle server writes nothing. The line does not name the model. The line is at info level, so a higher log level hides it. No command-line flag sets it. rinzler_proxy and rinzler_mock do not run this read: they have their own get_scheduler (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:87, src/tron/scheduler/mock.cpp:67).
variables.how_to_check: The log line itself: 'Completed <n> passes with <n> tokens for <n> logits in <seconds> s.  Throughput <x> tok/s.' at info level (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:235-240). No line while requests run means the value is unset or 0.
variables.audience_reason: A logging switch of the deployed scheduler: it turns on a periodic throughput line.

variables.name: TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT

readers.program: rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host and the tests that link the full or fake scheduler (inline function tron::get_prompt_chunk_size in h/libtron.hpp)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then std::stoul, in the initializer of a function-local static. Product callers: stream_generation_context::loop (src/tron/generation/context.cpp:42) and speculation_context::loop (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:481 and :506).

variables.values: Unsigned integer text parsed with std::stoul (base 10). The unit is tokens. Leading spaces are accepted and text after the digits is ignored.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. std::stoul throws std::invalid_argument on empty text, and the process ends (see invalid_value).
variables.invalid_value: Text that does not start with a number makes std::stoul throw. Both callers are declared noexcept (src/tron/generation/context.cpp:22, src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:460), so the exception ends the process. This happens when the first prompt is processed, not at startup. The code does not reject 0: with 0 each chunk has 0 tokens and prompt_tokens_processed does not advance (src/tron/generation/context.cpp:41-42 and :74-75). What the scheduler then does was not determined. A negative number was not determined: the result depends on the C library rule for strtoul, and the checkout has no test for it.
variables.effect: Sets the largest number of prompt tokens that one request hands to the scheduler in one step. A longer prompt is processed in several chunks of this size. Logits are requested only with the last chunk (src/tron/generation/context.cpp:41-75).
variables.interactions: With speculation the same limit is used for the target prompt and for the draft prompt (src/tron/generation/speculate.cpp:481 and :506). bin/analyze-tps:53-59 sets it together with TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT to select a scheduling strategy: 10000 for blast and queueing, 128 for chunk. t/CMakeLists.txt:526 sets 512 for one test. The value is read once per process and then kept. No command-line flag sets it. rinzler_proxy and rinzler_mock define their own stream_generate (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:381, src/tron/scheduler/mock.cpp:106) and never call the function.
variables.how_to_check: none found in product code. Only a test prints the value (t/t_kv_oom_persist_ephem.cpp:117).
variables.audience_reason: Scheduling and performance tuning of rinzler and runtron; the load-test script bin/analyze-tps sets it.

variables.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH

readers.program: every program that builds a tron::thread_pool. The shared app pool is built on the first call of app_pool() (h/tron/threading.hpp:745-759), and its constructor builds the speedometer (h/tron/threading.hpp:645).
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then std::atof, in the constructor of tron::speedometer_t
readers.when: every call of the speedometer_t constructor

variables.values: Floating-point text parsed with std::atof. It must be 0 or above. It is a ratio without a unit.
variables.empty_value: Parses as 0.0. That value is accepted: the pull toward the group mean is then off.
variables.invalid_value: Non-numeric text parses as 0.0 and is accepted without a message. A negative value fails TRON_ASSERT_GE at h/tron/threading.hpp:529 and the process aborts when the thread pool is built. TRON_ASSERT is active in every build type (h/common/assert.hpp:3-5 and :69-75). It logs the message, logs 'Aborting.' and calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:57-63).
variables.effect: Sets how strongly each worker's speed estimate is pulled toward the mean of all workers at each update. The factor is exp(-value / timescale) (h/tron/threading.hpp:531 and :553-572). 0 removes the pull. A larger value pulls harder.
variables.interactions: The timescale in the formula is TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE or its default 10. The speed estimates split the attention work between the attention workers (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2422-2446). With pay_for_determinism the estimates are not used (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2426-2431). The estimator is updated once for each attention plan, so once per forward pass (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2424 and :2678). No command-line flag sets it.
variables.how_to_check: No log line prints the value. When the pool is destroyed the info line 'Worker speeds: [...]' shows the estimates, not the setting (h/tron/threading.hpp:535). On a negative value the abort message is 'TRON_ASSERT((prior_strength) >= (0.0f)): Expected prior_strength >= 0.0f, but got <value> < 0.'
variables.audience_reason: A constant of an internal estimator. No document, script or test in the checkout names it, and a bad value aborts the process. The inventory says operator; that is a classification choice, not a fact error.

variables.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE

readers.program: every program that builds a tron::thread_pool. The shared app pool is built on the first call of app_pool() (h/tron/threading.hpp:745-759), and its constructor builds the speedometer (h/tron/threading.hpp:645).
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then std::atof, in the constructor of tron::speedometer_t
readers.when: every call of the speedometer_t constructor

variables.values: Floating-point text parsed with std::atof. It must be above 0. The unit is update steps of the estimator; there is one update per forward pass.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. Empty text parses as 0.0, the check 'above 0' fails, and the process aborts.
variables.invalid_value: Non-numeric text parses as 0.0. A value of 0 or below fails TRON_ASSERT_GT at h/tron/threading.hpp:528 and the process aborts when the thread pool is built. TRON_ASSERT is active in every build type (h/common/assert.hpp:3-5 and :69-75). It logs the message, logs 'Aborting.' and calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:57-63).
variables.effect: Sets the time constant of the per-worker speed estimator. At each update the old measurements are scaled by exp(-1 / value) (h/tron/threading.hpp:530 and :553-572). A larger value makes the estimate change more slowly.
variables.interactions: The value is also the divisor in the pull factor exp(-prior_strength / timescale) of TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH (h/tron/threading.hpp:531). The speed estimates split the attention work between the attention workers (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2422-2446). With pay_for_determinism the estimates are not used (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2426-2431). The estimator is updated once for each attention plan, so once per forward pass (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2424 and :2678). No command-line flag sets it.
variables.how_to_check: No log line prints the value. When the pool is destroyed the info line 'Worker speeds: [...]' shows the estimates, not the setting (h/tron/threading.hpp:535). On a value of 0 or below the abort message is 'TRON_ASSERT((timescale) > (0.0f)): Expected timescale > 0.0f, but got <value> <= 0.'
variables.audience_reason: A constant of an internal estimator. No document, script or test in the checkout names it, and a bad value aborts the process. The inventory says operator; that is a classification choice, not a fact error.

variables.name: TRON_TOKENIZE_PY

readers.program: librinzler (static library from src/rinzler/, linked into rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy, runtron and tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in fallback_tokenizer_program(). The constructor of the Python fallback tokenizer calls it (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:459).

variables.values: Path to the Python tokenizer program. A non-empty value is used as given; the text is not checked beyond 'the path exists'.
variables.default: Unset: the relative path bin/tokenize_py (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:453). The process resolves it against its current working directory.
variables.invalid_value: If the path does not exist, TRON_ASSERT at src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:462-465 aborts the process with 'Python tokenizer script <path> not found; run in the tron source directory or set TRON_TOKENIZE_PY.' The abort is not an exception, so the try block in make_python_tokenizer does not catch it (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1923-1929). If the program exists but fails, the constructor throws 'Python tokenizer subprocess failed ...' (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:476-480).
variables.effect: Selects the program that the Python fallback tokenizer starts as a child process to read the vocabulary and to encode text. The command is '<program> -n <model directory>' plus an option, started with popen (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:460 and :467-469).
variables.interactions: The variable matters only when a Python fallback tokenizer is built. That happens in three cases: the model directory has no tokenizer.json or the Rust tokenizer fails to load (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1891-1903); USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER is set and is not the text false (:2197-2204); VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS is set and is not the text false (:2193-2196 and :1940). The path is put into a shell command line without quotes. Outside product code: the make rule for gen/tokenize_py copies the file that the variable names when IN_NIX_SHELL is set (GNUmakefile:549-557); flake.nix:578 and :1924 set it in the Nix shells; bin/dice-lsf-runner:1408 sets it for test jobs. No command-line flag sets it.
variables.how_to_check: Warning log line each time a Python fallback tokenizer is built: 'Falling back to slow tokenizer script <path>' (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:461). The path in that line is the value in effect.
variables.audience_reason: A path that a deployed rinzler needs when it uses the Python fallback tokenizer; a wrong path aborts the process.

variables.name: TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES

readers.program: libpos and pos_fake (src/pos/perf.cpp is in both: rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv(trace_categories_variable) in trace_categories_spec(). The constant holds the name (h/common/perfetto.hpp:243). Callers: require_no_trace_category_override (src/pos/perf.cpp:127) and local_trace_config (src/pos/perf.cpp:144, only when the caller gives no category text).

variables.values: Comma-separated list of entries. Each entry is +name (record the category) or -name (do not record it). A name is a registered category, or the start of one followed by *. The text is not trimmed, so a space makes an entry bad. Registered categories (h/common/perfetto.hpp:103-138): rinzler, sys, scheduler, model, model-moe, matmul, loading, driver, driver-detail, gen, hwattention, hwattention-detail, hw, memory.
variables.default: Unset: no category selection is put in the trace config, so the Perfetto defaults apply (src/pos/perf.cpp:143-149). The comment at h/common/perfetto.hpp:245-249 says a category is then recorded unless it is tagged debug or slow; driver-detail is tagged slow and memory is tagged debug.
variables.invalid_value: A bad entry makes the trace start throw std::invalid_argument. Bad means: empty entry, no + or - sign, no name, a * that is not at the end, or a name that matches no registered category (src/pos/perf.cpp:92-124). The text of the error is 'TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES: entry "<entry>" <reason>. Expected a comma-separated list of +name or -name, where name is one of [...]' (src/pos/perf.cpp:82-90). What follows depends on the caller: see interactions.
variables.effect: Selects which trace categories an in-process trace records. An in-process trace is one that the process writes to a file itself: runtron --trace FILE, runtron --trace-gen FILE (with or without --trace-passes), a SIGUSR1 capture when TRACE_FILE names a file, and a FUSE capture that gives no category text of its own.
variables.interactions: Destination traced (the Perfetto daemon; the default when TRACE_FILE is unset): a set, non-empty value makes start_tracing throw, because the daemon takes its categories from its own config file (src/pos/perf.cpp:126-134 and :165). The SIGUSR1 capture thread is noexcept and has no try block (src/pos/perf.cpp:248 and :273), so there the throw ends the process. This covers a SIGUSR1 sent to a rinzler that has the variable set and no TRACE_FILE, and a SIGUSR1 capture to a file with a bad value. The runtron trace thread for --trace and --trace-gen also has no try block (src/runtron.cpp:331-342). A FUSE capture catches the error and reports a failed capture with the error text (src/pos/trace_capture.cpp:585 and :599-603). A FUSE capture that passes its own categories does not read the variable (src/pos/trace_capture.cpp:460-461, src/pos/perf.cpp:143-145). The value is read at each trace start, not once. The tool perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:196-207 reads the variable from /proc/<pid>/environ of the target rinzler and refuses to send SIGUSR1 when it is set.
variables.how_to_check: none found: no log line prints the selection. A bad value shows up as the error text above. For a running rinzler the capture tool reads /proc/<pid>/environ (perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:196-207).
variables.audience_reason: It only changes what a Perfetto trace records. A support engineer must still know one rule: a rinzler that can get SIGUSR1 must run with it unset.
variables.disagreement: Missing, not wrong. The owning entry (cpp-pos-system.json) lists the affected traces as runtron --trace FILE, a SIGUSR1 capture to a file, and a FUSE capture. It leaves out runtron --trace-gen FILE and the --trace-passes path. The code reads the variable there too: src/runtron.cpp:336 and :267 call start_tracing, which calls local_trace_config (src/pos/perf.cpp:180). The cross-area entry in cpp-rinzler-runtron.json has both. The merge note says to take the owning text, so the merged text would lose them.

variables.name: TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN

readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then atoi and std::max with 0, in the initializer of a function-local static in trace_from_token()
std::getenv, tested only for being set, when --trace-passes is given. It only decides whether a warning is logged.

variables.values: Integer text parsed with atoi. The unit is tokens: prompt tokens plus generated tokens of one request. A negative result is raised to 0 (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:64).
variables.default: Unset: 0. The trace starts when prompt parsing completes (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:823-824).
variables.empty_value: Parses as 0, same as unset for the trace start. The second read tests only that the variable is set, so an empty value still gives the --trace-passes warning.
variables.invalid_value: Non-numeric text parses as 0. No message.
variables.effect: With runtron --trace-gen FILE (phased tracing), the trace start waits until one request has prompt tokens plus generated tokens at or above the value (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:836-840). A value at or below the prompt length starts the trace at parse completion. The comment at h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:53-60 says this keeps the trace of a very long run small.
variables.interactions: Only --trace-gen without --trace-passes uses the value. With --trace-passes the value has no effect, because that path installs no phase callback (src/runtron.cpp:252-281), and runtron logs a warning. With --trace (whole run) the phase callback acts only on phase 1, so the value has no effect (src/runtron.cpp:316-323). If no request reaches the value, the start phase does not fire; the end phase of the first finished request then opens and closes the trace at once (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:541, src/runtron.cpp:296-315). The value is kept after the first use, so set it before the process starts. rinzler does not read this variable.
variables.how_to_check: Only with --trace-passes: warning line '--trace-passes overrides TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN' (src/runtron.cpp:550). No log line prints the value.
variables.audience_reason: It only moves the start of a runtron Perfetto trace.

variables.name: TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR

readers.program: libsystem (linked into rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host and tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then strcmp with 1, in read_arena_allocator_env(). Two callers. 1. pos_heap_setup (src/system/memory.cpp:174), run once in pos_startup_host of the real device library (src/pos/driver.cpp:290): it fixes the allocator for the process. 2. pos_heap_register_fuse_stats (src/system/memory.cpp:535), called at src/rinzler.cpp:4957 and src/runtron.cpp:501: it reads the variable again.

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 selects the arena allocator (pos_heap_v2). Every other set value selects the legacy allocator (pos_heap) (src/system/memory.cpp:94-96).
variables.default: Unset: the build default. The CMake option TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON is ON by default (src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86-89), so a default build uses the arena allocator. No preset, makefile, Nix file or packaging file in the checkout changes that option.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. An empty value is set and is not the text 1, so it selects the legacy allocator.
variables.invalid_value: Every text other than exactly 1 selects the legacy allocator, for example 0, true, yes, on, 2, or 1 followed by a space. No warning is printed.
variables.effect: Selects the allocator of the DMA heap (the hugepage memory that the FPGA cards read and write). Arena mode also turns on these parts: the FUSE stats files under /rinzler/stats/dma_heap/ (src/system/memory.cpp:521-536); the memory-pressure stats and the eviction target of rinzler (src/rinzler.cpp:4383-4385, src/system/memory.cpp:195-205); the evict-before-fail rescue on allocation failure (src/tron/scheduler/full.cpp:343-344). In arena mode the static KV cache sizes are ignored, with one warning for each one supplied (h/tron/scheduler/token_cache_policy.hpp:21-30).
variables.interactions: RZ_KV_CACHE_GB, --kv-cache-gb and --kv-cache-bytes are ignored in arena mode. TRON_HEAP_SHADOW and --heap-shadow have an effect only in arena mode (src/system/memory.cpp:175-183). In runtron the second read runs before pos_heap_setup (src/runtron.cpp:501). The pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host) never call pos_heap_setup; for them the variable changes only whether the dma_heap stats files are registered. Other code reads the fixed choice through pos_heap_is_arena_allocator (src/system/memory.cpp:287-289). No command-line flag selects the allocator.
variables.how_to_check: Arena mode: info log line 'pos_heap_setup: using arena allocator (pos_heap_v2)', with ' with shadow map' added when the shadow map is on (src/system/memory.cpp:182-183). Legacy mode prints no line. Second check: the files under /rinzler/stats/dma_heap/ in the FUSE stats tree exist only when the variable selects the arena allocator.
variables.audience_reason: It selects the memory allocator and the memory pressure behaviour of a deployed rinzler.

variables.name: TRON_USE_SPECULATION

readers.program: rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host and the tests that link the full or fake scheduler (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp is part of the full and fake scheduler libraries)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then std::atoi, in the initializer of the namespace-scope constant prefer_eagle. get_scheduler uses the constant (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:59).

variables.values: Integer text parsed with std::atoi. Any non-zero result turns it on: 1, 2, a negative number, or text that starts with digits such as 1x. 0 leaves it off.
variables.empty_value: Parses as 0: off, same as unset.
variables.invalid_value: Non-numeric text such as true, yes or on parses as 0: off. No message is printed.
variables.effect: When on, get_scheduler looks for a compiled-in model named eagle-<model id> for each model it loads. If that name is not registered, it removes the parts -good, -fast, -nice and -best and looks again. If a model is found, get_scheduler sets support_eagle in the model config, loads the EAGLE model with 1 layer from its default path, and attaches it as a draft scheduler (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:28-81). rinzler then generates with speculative decoding (src/rinzler.cpp:3380, src/tron/scheduler/full.cpp:357-362, src/tron/generation.cpp:51-56). If no EAGLE model is registered, nothing changes and nothing is logged.
variables.interactions: rinzler with an attached draft answers HTTP 400 to four kinds of request: logprobs (when the model slug does not start with gemma), structured output, tool calling, and reasoning_budget_tokens (src/rinzler.cpp:3229-3305). runtron: without --draft-model, runtron removes the speculator again (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:682-691), so the variable only loads and attaches the EAGLE model and runtron does not speculate. runtron --draft-model eagle sets support_eagle itself (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1475) and uses the draft (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:973-974); with that flag and no EAGLE model the process aborts with 'No EAGLE model found for <model>' (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:82-85). The variable alone never aborts. A config with support_eagle is rejected for pipeline stages: 'EAGLE speculation does not support pipeline stages' (h/tron/models/model.hpp:893-894). The value is read before main (or when the scheduler library is loaded), so it must be in the environment when the process starts. The draft tree is tuned with TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_SIZE, TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH and TRON_DRAFT_TREE_MAX_WIDTH. rinzler_proxy and rinzler_mock do not run this read: they have their own get_scheduler (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:87, src/tron/scheduler/mock.cpp:67).
variables.how_to_check: Info log line when an EAGLE model is found, once per model name: 'Found EAGLE model for <model>: <eagle model>' (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:45). There is no line when the variable is on and no EAGLE model is registered. In rinzler the HTTP 400 texts '... is not supported with speculation' also show that a draft is attached.
variables.audience_reason: A feature switch of the deployed server: it turns on speculative decoding and makes rinzler reject four kinds of request.
variables.disagreement: Partly wrong and partly missing. 1. The inventory says that with a found EAGLE model 'generation uses speculative decoding'. That holds for rinzler. runtron removes the speculator unless --draft-model is given (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:679-691), so in runtron the variable alone does not make generation speculate. 2. Missing: rinzler with speculation on answers HTTP 400 to logprobs (non-gemma models), structured output, tool calling and reasoning_budget_tokens (src/rinzler.cpp:3229-3305). 3. Missing: the log line 'Found EAGLE model for ...' (src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:45) and the runtron flag --draft-model eagle that sets support_eagle (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1475).

variables.name: TZ

readers.program: librinzler through the minijinja_ffi crate (linked into rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy, runtron and tests)
readers.mechanism: implicit read by the C library: libc::localtime_r in strftime_now gives the local UTC offset. Product code never calls getenv for TZ.

readers.program: librinzler (linked into rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy, runtron and tests)
readers.mechanism: implicit read by the C library: localtime_r in format_system_date

readers.program: librinzler (linked into rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy, runtron and tests)
readers.mechanism: implicit read by the C library: std::mktime in parse_system_start_date

variables.values: A time zone setting for the C library. TRON code does not parse it. The only value in the checkout is the POSIX rule string of a Rust unit test (rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs:891).
variables.default: not determined: the checkout has no rule for the unset case. The C library chooses the time zone (rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs:88, src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:940).
variables.empty_value: not determined: the C library decides. The checkout has no code and no test for an empty TZ.
variables.invalid_value: not determined: the C library decides how it reads a bad zone text. If localtime_r fails, strftime_now returns the error 'invalid render timestamp' (rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs:76-90) and format_system_date throws 'localtime_r failed to format system date' (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:940-942).
variables.effect: Changes the local date that rinzler writes into prompts. 1. strftime_now() in chat templates takes its UTC offset from localtime_r (rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs:74-106). 2. The Harmony system message gets conversation_start_date from today's local date (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:953-958 and :1085). 3. The rendered_at field of a save_tokens capture uses the same local date (src/rinzler/hf-token-processor.cpp:686). 4. A date pinned with RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE is taken as local noon through mktime (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:966-992).
variables.interactions: RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE pins the date, and then the wall clock is not used (src/rinzler/hf-token-processor.cpp:677-682, src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:953-957). The comment at rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs:70-73 says the Rust side takes the offset from the C library so that it renders the same date as the C++ side. The test comment at rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs:887-888 says glibc reads TZ only once, so set it before the process starts. The only explicit read and the only setter are in the Rust unit test (rust/minijinja/src/lib.rs:892 and :908, inside the test module that starts at :631). Not verified: the log pattern uses %H:%M:%S with no time type (src/system/spdlog.cpp:69-70 and :86-89); spdlog is not in the checkout, so the link between TZ and log timestamps could not be checked.
variables.how_to_check: none found in the logs. The rendered_at field of a save_tokens capture holds the local date in effect (src/rinzler/hf-token-processor.cpp:686).
variables.audience_reason: It changes the date text in the prompts of a deployed rinzler, so the prompt tokens can differ near midnight.

notes: Method. Step 1 was done from the code before the inventory files were opened. Step 2 compared each entry and re-read the code where the two differed. Nothing in the checkout was changed, built or run. Result. 12 of 14 entries agree with the code in every stated fact. Two entries need a change: TRON_USE_SPECULATION (the effect text is wrong for runtron and lacks the HTTP 400 rules of rinzler) and TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES (the owning entry leaves out runtron --trace-gen and --trace-passes). Meaning of agrees_with_inventory here: false when the inventory states something wrong, or leaves out a fact that changes what a support engineer would do. The disagreement text says which of the two. TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE: the task text says product code reads all 14 names. For this name that is not so at commit 7eddde7895: the reader is defined in a product header, but only the test t/t_prequant_cache.cpp includes the header and calls the reader. The inventory already says this, and its audience 'test' is right. Where the inventory was more exact than the blind pass: TRON_NO_RTM is not read at all on a CPU without RTM (short-circuit at src/system/mwaitx.cpp:58). The blind pass missed that; the code confirms the inventory. Facts added here that the inventory lacks, none of them a contradiction. TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS and TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS: the limits also apply with pay_for_determinism, and the code comment says a changed split changes the exact logits; no log line shows the values. TRON_PERF_INTERVAL_SEC and TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT: a bad value ends the process at the first request, not at startup. TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN: when no request reaches the value, the trace is opened and closed at the end of the first finished request. TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR and TRON_TOKENIZE_PY: the exact log lines that show the value in effect. Audience. TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE and TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH are marked developer-debug here and operator in the inventory. This is a classification choice: the task text puts performance tuning under operator, but nothing in the checkout documents or sets these two names. Format remark on the inventory. Some reader rows are call sites that do not read the variable themselves, for example src/rinzler.cpp:4044 and src/runtron.cpp:247 for TRON_NO_RTM in cpp-rinzler-runtron.json, and h/tron/models/model.hpp:1614 and :1615 in cpp-tron.json. The rows say so in their mechanism text, but the field rule asks that every site really reads the name. Not determined. TZ: default, empty and bad values are decided by the C library, which is not in the checkout. TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT: the behaviour for 0 after the first empty chunk, and for a negative number. No in-scope variable was met in this code that is absent from the inventory files.
